reason: The chapter says the catalyst cartridge fits the emptied retort, making it the natural first reactor assembly step.
expectation: The cartridge will prepare the retort for the methane-producing reaction.

effect: The retort now has a clean catalyst gas path; it still needs the process frame for the controlled reactor.
reaction: The separate inserts make the changeover from ore processing clear.
reason: The frame was built to support the reactor vessel, so mounting the catalyzed retort is the next logical step.
expectation: The retort will be mounted in the process frame to form the controlled reactor.

effect: The reactor is mounted and controlled, with hydrogen connected and a separate CO₂ inlet ready.
reaction: The explanation of both heating and cooling clarified the reactor's controls.
reason: The compressed carbon dioxide is the available feed for the marked inlet, and hydrogen is already connected.
expectation: The reactor will use the two gases to produce contained methane.

effect: The commissioning run produced methane, but its water vapour and unreacted gases mean it is not yet ready for a rocket tank. The chapter is complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to reach methane without treating the first output as finished fuel.

mostWorthwhile.text: Mounting the retort was most worthwhile: the explanation of metering, startup heating and reaction cooling made the reactor feel like more than a simple recipe.

leastWorthwhile.text: Changing the retort insert was the least engaging passage, though the clean gas path gave it a clear practical purpose.

surprise.text: I appreciated that the first run produced an impure test sample rather than immediately usable rocket fuel; that changed my understanding of how much remains after synthesis.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary: the cartridge, support frame and carbon-dioxide feed each had a stated role.

continue.text: Yes. I would choose to see how the methane is purified and how the discovery gets home; the reactor sequence made those next steps feel consequential.
